jsDoc.doc:
Compare two ChronVers.

Versions are ordered by year, month, day and changeset. When those match, a
`-break` version sorts after one without it.

The feature is ignored, like build metadata in SemVer: `2024.04.03-a`,
`2024.04.03-b` and `2024.04.03` all compare equal.

Returns `0` if `version1` equals `version2`, or `1` if `version1` is greater, or `-1` if `version2` is
greater.

Sorts in ascending order if passed to {@linkcode Array.sort}.

tags.doc: `1` if `version1` is greater, `0` if equal, or `-1` if `version2` is greater

jsDoc.doc:
Returns `true` if both ChronVers are equivalent.

This is equal to `compare(version1, version2) === 0`.

The feature is ignored, like build metadata in SemVer: `2024.04.03-a` equals
`2024.04.03-b` and `2024.04.03`.

Formats a ChronVer object into a string.

The year is padded to 4 digits and a changeset of `0` is omitted, so
`format(parse(s)) === s` for every string {@linkcode parse} accepts. The
version is validated first, so whatever this returns parses back to the
same version.

tags.doc: If the version is invalid: see {@linkcode isChronVer} for the rules.
The string representation of the ChronVer

jsDoc.doc:
Creates a ChronVer from a date, using the date's local time.

A changeset of `0` is omitted when formatted.

tags.doc: If the date is invalid, its year is outside 1 to 9999, or the changeset isn't a non-negative integer.

jsDoc.doc:
Greater than or equal to comparison for two ChronVers.

This is equal to `compare(version1, version2) >= 0`.

tags.doc: `true` if `version1` is greater than or equal to `version2`, `false` otherwise

jsDoc.doc:
Greater than comparison for two ChronVers.

This is equal to `compare(version1, version2) > 0`.

Returns the next version on the given date, in local time.

If the version is from the same day, its changeset goes up by one.
If it's from an earlier day, the result is that date's version with
changeset `0`. Either way the result has no feature and isn't breaking, so
`2024.04.03.1-break` becomes `2024.04.03.2` on the same day.

tags.doc: If the version's date is later than `date`, or `date` is invalid or outside the years 1 to 9999.

tags.name: date
tags.doc: The date of the new version

jsDoc.doc:
Checks to see if value is a valid ChronVer object: one that
{@linkcode format} accepts and that {@linkcode parse} reads back unchanged.
The year must be from 1 to 9999, the date a real calendar date and the
changeset a non-negative safe integer. The feature, if present, may only
contain letters, digits and hyphens (not only hyphens), can't be `break`,
and can't be combined with `isBreaking`.

Objects which are valid ChronVer objects but have _extra_ fields are still
considered ChronVer objects and this will return true.

A type assertion is added to the value.

tags.name: value
tags.doc: The value to check to see if it's a valid ChronVer object
`true` if value is a valid ChronVer, `false` otherwise

jsDoc.doc:
Less than or equal to comparison for two ChronVers.

This is equal to `compare(version1, version2) <= 0`.

tags.doc: `true` if `version1` is less than or equal to `version2`, `false` otherwise

jsDoc.doc:
Less than comparison for two ChronVers.

This is equal to `compare(version1, version2) < 0`.

Parses a string as a ChronVer, returning a ChronVer object.

The format is `YYYY.MM.DD[.CHANGESET][-FEATURE|-break]`. The date must be
a real calendar date, so `2024.02.29` is valid but `2023.02.29` is not.
The changeset is optional, but when present it's a positive integer with no
leading zeros. A version is either a feature or `-break`, not both: in
`2024.04.03-ui-break` the feature is `ui-break`.

Every string this accepts formats back to itself with {@linkcode format}.

tags.doc: If the input string is invalid.

jsDoc.doc:
Sorts ChronVer strings, returning a new array.

Versions that compare equal keep their input order.

tags.doc: If any string is not a valid ChronVer.

jsDoc.doc: Returns the parsed ChronVer, or `undefined` if it's not valid.

A ChronVer object parsed into its constituent parts.

A ChronVer string has the format `YYYY.MM.DD[.CHANGESET][-FEATURE|-break]`.
The year
The month, from 1 to 12
The day of the month, from 1 to 31
The changeset number, `0` if not specified
The feature name, if specified
Whether this is a breaking change (`-break`)
